title: Generics are puzzling. Can language models find the missing piece?

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating implicit quantification of generic sentences expressing positive and negative stereotypes about real and invented social groups using a surprisal-based 'p-acceptability' metric to measure if models overgeneralize.
Applying the 'p-acceptability' metric to determine the implicit quantification of generic sentences containing political stereotypes (e.g., 'liberals are corrupt', 'democrats are cheaters').

Applying the 'p-acceptability' metric to evaluate the implicit quantification of culturally and nationally based generic stereotypes (e.g., 'spaniards love gazpacho', 'germans celebrate with lederhosen').
Measuring the implicit quantification of positive and negative generic statements generated about different races using the surprisal-based 'p-acceptability' metric.
Measuring the implicit quantification of positive and negative generic statements generated about different religions using the surprisal-based 'p-acceptability' metric.
